222	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
223	# Per-function conversion
224	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
225	
226	
227	class _Converter:
228	    def __init__(self, func: Function):
229	        self.func = func
230	        self.cfg = _CFG(func)
231	        self._fresh_counter = 0
232	
233	    def fresh(self, typ: str) -> Temp:
234	        temp = Temp(self._fresh_counter, typ)
235	        self._fresh_counter += 1
236	        return temp
237	
238	    def convert(self) -> Function:
239	        cfg = self.cfg
240	        entry = self.func.entry
241	        idom = _dominators(cfg, entry)
242	        frontiers = _dominance_frontiers(cfg, idom)
243	
244	        new_blocks = [Block(block.id) for block in cfg.blocks]
245	        block_map = dict(zip(cfg.blocks, new_blocks))
246	
247	        # -- definition sites, in original DFS definition order ----------
248	        param_temp: dict = {}
249	        defs: dict[object, list[Block]] = {}
250	        ref_order: dict[object, int] = {}
251	
252	        def register(ref, block: Block) -> None:
253	            if ref not in ref_order:
254	                ref_order[ref] = len(ref_order)
255	            defs.setdefault(ref, []).append(block)
256	
257	        for param in self.func.params:
258	            temp = self.fresh(param.slot.type)
259	            param_temp[param.slot] = temp
260	            register(param.slot, entry)
261	
262	        for block in cfg.blocks:
263	            if block not in cfg.reachable:
264	                continue
265	            for ins in block.instructions:
266	                register(ins.dest, block)
267	
268	        # -- phi placeholders at iterated dominance frontiers ------------
269	        phi_origin: dict[Phi, object] = {}
270	        block_phis: dict[Block, list[Phi]] = {}
271	        already: dict[Block, set[object]] = {
272	            block: set() for block in cfg.reachable
273	        }
274	        for ref in sorted(ref_order, key=lambda r: ref_order[r]):
275	            worklist = list(defs[ref])
276	            while worklist:
277	                site = worklist.pop()
278	                for frontier in frontiers.get(site, ()):
279	                    if ref in already[frontier]:
280	                        continue
281	                    already[frontier].add(ref)
282	                    phi = Phi(self.fresh(ref.type), {})
283	                    phi_origin[phi] = ref
284	                    block_phis.setdefault(frontier, []).append(phi)
285	                    if not any(s is frontier for s in worklist):
286	                        worklist.append(frontier)
287	
288	        for block in block_phis:
289	            block_phis[block].sort(key=lambda phi: ref_order[phi_origin[phi]])
290	
291	        # -- renaming over the dominator tree ----------------------------
292	        stacks: dict[object, list[Temp]] = {
293	            slot: [temp] for slot, temp in param_temp.items()
294	        }
295	
296	        children: dict[Block, list[Block]] = {
297	            block: [] for block in cfg.reachable
298	        }
299	        for block in cfg.sort(cfg.reachable):
300	            if block is not entry:
301	                children[idom[block]].append(block)
302	        for child_list in children.values():
303	            child_list.sort(key=lambda b: cfg.index[b])
304	
305	        def top(ref):
306	            stack = stacks.get(ref)
307	            return stack[-1] if stack else None
308	
309	        loose: dict[object, Temp] = {}
310	
311	        def use(ref):
312	            mapped = top(ref)
313	            if mapped is None:
314	                # Only reached on edges where the name is genuinely
315	                # undefined; in lowered IR such edges are unreachable, and
316	                # the placeholder disappears together with its dead phi.
317	                mapped = loose.get(ref)
318	                if mapped is None:
319	                    mapped = self.fresh(ref.type)
320	                    loose[ref] = mapped
321	            return mapped
322	
323	        def rename(old: Block, new: Block) -> None:
324	            saved = {ref: len(stack) for ref, stack in stacks.items()}
325	
326	            for phi in block_phis.get(old, ()):
327	                stacks.setdefault(phi_origin[phi], []).append(phi.dest)
328	
329	            for ins in old.instructions:
330	                if isinstance(ins, Copy):
331	                    # A copy is pure aliasing in SSA: the defined name now
332	                    # denotes the renamed source value, no instruction (and
333	                    # no fresh definition) is emitted.  This is also what
334	                    # lets branches assigning the same value share one SSA
335	                    # value and keep their merge phi trivial.
336	                    stacks.setdefault(ins.dest, []).append(use(ins.src))
337	                    continue
338	                cloned = self._clone_ins(ins, use)
339	                new.instructions.append(cloned)
340	                stacks.setdefault(ins.dest, []).append(cloned.dest)
341	
342	            new.terminator = self._clone_terminator(old.terminator,
343	                                                    block_map, use)
344	
345	            # Fill the phi of every reachable successor: current block is
346	            # the predecessor supplying top(ref) on this edge.
347	            for successor in cfg.succs[old]:
348	                if successor not in cfg.reachable:
349	                    continue
350	                for phi in block_phis.get(successor, ()):
351	                    phi.entries[new] = use(phi_origin[phi])
352	
353	            for child in children[old]:
354	                rename(child, block_map[child])
355	
356	            for ref, length in saved.items():
357	                del stacks[ref][length:]
358	
359	        rename(entry, block_map[entry])
360	
361	        for old, new in block_map.items():
362	            new.phis = list(block_phis.get(old, ()))
363	            if old not in cfg.reachable:
364	                self._clone_unreachable(old, new, block_map)
365	
366	        new_params = [
367	            Parameter(param.name, param.slot, param_temp[param.slot])
368	            for param in self.func.params
369	        ]
370	        self._prune(new_blocks)
371	        self._renumber(new_params, new_blocks)
372	
373	        return Function(
374	            self.func.name,
375	            new_params,
376	            self.func.ret_type,
377	            [],
378	            new_blocks,
379	            block_map[entry],
380	            ssa=True,
381	        )
382	
383	    # -- cloning -----------------------------------------------------------
384	
385	    def _clone_ins(self, ins, use):
386	        if isinstance(ins, Const):
387	            return Const(self.fresh(ins.dest.type), ins.value)
388	        if isinstance(ins, Copy):
389	            return Copy(self.fresh(ins.dest.type), use(ins.src))
390	        if isinstance(ins, BinOp):
391	            return BinOp(
392	                self.fresh(ins.dest.type), ins.operator,
393	                use(ins.left), use(ins.right), ins.kind, ins.type,
394	            )
395	        return Call(
396	            self.fresh(ins.dest.type), ins.name,
397	            [use(arg) for arg in ins.args], ins.type,
398	        )
399	
400	    def _clone_terminator(self, term, block_map, use):
401	        if isinstance(term, Return):
402	            return Return(None if term.value is None else use(term.value))
403	        if isinstance(term, Jump):
404	            return Jump(block_map[term.target])
405	        if isinstance(term, Branch):
406	            return Branch(
407	                use(term.cond),
408	                block_map[term.true_target],
409	                block_map[term.false_target],
410	            )
411	        return None  # pragma: no cover - lowerer always terminates blocks
412	
413	    def _clone_unreachable(self, old: Block, new: Block, block_map) -> None:
414	        """Structural clone for blocks unreachable from the entry.
415	
416	        ``lower_module`` never emits such blocks; this keeps the transform
417	        total without inserting phi nodes that no reachable edge feeds.
418	        """
419	        local: dict[object, Temp] = {}
420	
421	        def local_use(ref):
422	            mapped = local.get(ref)
423	            if mapped is None:
424	                mapped = self.fresh(ref.type)
425	                local[ref] = mapped
426	            return mapped
427	
428	        new.phis = []
429	        new.instructions = []
430	        for ins in old.instructions:
431	            if isinstance(ins, Copy):
432	                local[ins.dest] = local_use(ins.src)
433	                continue
434	            cloned = self._clone_ins(ins, local_use)
435	            local[ins.dest] = cloned.dest
436	            new.instructions.append(cloned)
437	        new.terminator = self._clone_terminator(
438	            old.terminator, block_map, local_use
439	        )
440	
441	    # -- phi pruning -------------------------------------------------------
442	
443	    def _prune(self, blocks: list[Block]) -> None:
444	        """Remove dead and trivial phi nodes to a fixpoint.
445	
446	        A phi is *dead* when nothing outside the phi-only reference graph
447	        reads its result: phi-only cycles (e.g. a loop-carried temporary
448	        nobody reads) evaporate together.  A phi is *trivial* when its
449	        incoming values collapse to one distinct value once previously
450	        removed phis are chased through; a loop self-reference on its own
451	        result counts as such.  Dead phis are dropped as a batch first,
452	        then trivial phis one at a time; the two passes alternate until
453	        neither fires.
454	        """
455	        while self._remove_dead_phis(blocks) | self._remove_trivial_phis(
456	            blocks
457	        ):
458	            pass
459	
460	    def _live_phi_dests(self, blocks: list[Block]) -> set[int]:
461	        all_phis = [phi for block in blocks for phi in block.phis]
462	
463	        # Worklist starts from temps consumed by ordinary instructions and
464	        # terminators; reaching a phi's result marks that phi live and in
465	        # turn activates the phis feeding it.  A closed phi-only cycle is
466	        # never seeded and so dies wholesale.
467	        worklist: list[int] = []
468	        for block in blocks:
469	            for ins in block.instructions:
470	                worklist.extend(id(v) for v in _operands(ins))
471	            worklist.extend(id(v) for v in _term_operands(block.terminator))
472	
473	        live: set[int] = set()
474	        phi_by_dest = {id(phi.dest): phi for phi in all_phis}
475	        while worklist:
476	            temp_id = worklist.pop()
477	            if temp_id in live:
478	                continue
479	            live.add(temp_id)
480	            phi = phi_by_dest.get(temp_id)
481	            if phi is not None:
482	                for value in phi.entries.values():
483	                    if value is not None and value is not phi.dest:
484	                        worklist.append(id(value))
485	        return live
486	
487	    def _remove_dead_phis(self, blocks: list[Block]) -> bool:
488	        live = self._live_phi_dests(blocks)
489	        changed = False
490	        for block in blocks:
491	            for phi in list(block.phis):
492	                if id(phi.dest) not in live:
493	                    block.phis.remove(phi)
494	                    changed = True
495	        return changed
496	
497	    def _remove_trivial_phis(self, blocks: list[Block]) -> bool:
498	        representative: dict[Temp, Temp] = {}
499	
500	        def canonical(value: Temp) -> Temp:
501	            seen = set()
502	            while value in representative and id(value) not in seen:
503	                seen.add(id(value))
504	                value = representative[value]
505	            return value
506	
507	        for block in blocks:
508	            for phi in list(block.phis):
509	                incoming = {
510	                    canonical(value)
511	                    for value in phi.entries.values()
512	                    if value is not None and value is not phi.dest
513	                }
514	                if len(incoming) == 1:
515	                    replacement = next(iter(incoming))
516	                    representative[phi.dest] = replacement
517	                    block.phis.remove(phi)
518	                    self._replace(blocks, phi.dest, replacement)
519	                    return True
520	        return False
521	
522	    def _replace(self, blocks: list[Block], old: Temp, new: Temp) -> None:
523	        def subst(value):
524	            return new if value is old else value
525	
526	        for block in blocks:
527	            for phi in block.phis:
528	                phi.entries = {
529	                    pred: subst(value) for pred, value in phi.entries.items()
530	                }
531	            for ins in block.instructions:
532	                _map_operands(ins, subst)
533	            _map_term_operands(block.terminator, subst)
534	
535	    # -- canonical numbering ----------------------------------------------
536	
537	    def _renumber(
538	        self, params: list[Parameter], blocks: list[Block]
539	    ) -> None:
540	        """Assign deterministic per-function SSA ids in place.
541	
542	        Parameters take ids first in parameter order; within each block
543	        (visited in id order) phi results precede ordinary instruction
544	        results.  Everything after renumbering refers to the new temps.
545	        """
546	        number: dict[Temp, Temp] = {}
547	        next_id = 0
548	
549	        def assign(temp: Temp) -> Temp:
550	            nonlocal next_id
551	            mapped = number.get(temp)
552	            if mapped is None:
553	                mapped = Temp(next_id, temp.type)
554	                next_id += 1
555	                number[temp] = mapped
556	            return mapped
557	
558	        for param in params:
559	            param.temp = assign(param.temp)
560	
561	        for block in blocks:
562	            for phi in block.phis:
563	                assign(phi.dest)
564	            for ins in block.instructions:
565	                assign(ins.dest)
566	
567	        def numbered(value):
568	            if value is None:
569	                return None
570	            mapped = number.get(value)
571	            if mapped is None:
572	                # Defensive: an operand with no reachable definition.
573	                # Never occurs for lowered, pruned IR.
574	                mapped = assign(value)
575	            return mapped
576	
577	        for block in blocks:
578	            for phi in block.phis:
579	                dest = numbered(phi.dest)
580	                phi.entries = {
581	                    pred: numbered(value)
582	                    for pred, value in sorted(
583	                        phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id
584	                    )
585	                }
586	                phi.dest = dest
587	            for ins in block.instructions:
588	                ins.dest = numbered(ins.dest)
589	                _map_operands(ins, numbered)
590	            _map_term_operands(block.terminator, numbered)
591	
592	
593	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
594	# Idempotent cloning of an already-SSA module
595	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
596	
597	
598	def _clone_ssa_module(module: Module) -> Module:
599	    return Module(
600	        [_clone_ssa_function(func) for func in module.functions], ssa=True
601	    )
602	
603	
604	def _clone_ssa_function(func: Function) -> Function:
605	    new_blocks = [Block(block.id) for block in func.blocks]
606	    block_map = dict(zip(func.blocks, new_blocks))
607	
608	    number: dict[Temp, Temp] = {}
609	    next_id = 0
610	
611	    def assign(temp: Temp) -> Temp:
612	        nonlocal next_id
613	        mapped = number.get(temp)
614	        if mapped is None:
615	            mapped = Temp(next_id, temp.type)
616	            next_id += 1
617	            number[temp] = mapped
618	        return mapped
619	
620	    new_params: list[Parameter] = []
621	    for param in func.params:
622	        new_params.append(
623	            Parameter(param.name, param.slot, assign(param.temp))
624	        )
625	    for block, new_block in zip(func.blocks, new_blocks):
626	        for phi in block.phis:
627	            assign(phi.dest)
628	        for ins in block.instructions:
629	            assign(ins.dest)
630	
631	    def ref(value):
632	        return number[value] if value is not None else None
633	
634	    for block, new_block in zip(func.blocks, new_blocks):
635	        for phi in block.phis:
636	            entries = {
637	                block_map[pred]: ref(value)
638	                for pred, value in sorted(
639	                    phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id
640	                )
641	            }
642	            new_block.phis.append(Phi(ref(phi.dest), entries))
643	        for ins in block.instructions:
644	            if isinstance(ins, Const):
645	                clone = Const(ref(ins.dest), ins.value)
646	            elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
647	                clone = Copy(ref(ins.dest), ref(ins.src))
648	            elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
649	                clone = BinOp(
650	                    ref(ins.dest), ins.operator, ref(ins.left),
651	                    ref(ins.right), ins.kind, ins.type,
652	                )
653	            else:
654	                clone = Call(
655	                    ref(ins.dest), ins.name,
656	                    [ref(arg) for arg in ins.args], ins.type,
657	                )
658	            new_block.instructions.append(clone)
659	        term = block.terminator
660	        if isinstance(term, Return):
661	            new_block.terminator = Return(ref(term.value))
662	        elif isinstance(term, Jump):
663	            new_block.terminator = Jump(block_map[term.target])
664	        elif isinstance(term, Branch):
665	            new_block.terminator = Branch(
666	                ref(term.cond),
667	                block_map[term.true_target],
668	                block_map[term.false_target],
669	            )
670	
671	    return Function(
672	        func.name,
673	        new_params,
674	        func.ret_type,
675	        list(func.locals),
676	        new_blocks,
677	        block_map[func.entry],
678	        ssa=True,
679	    )
680

1	"""The control-flow IR object model.
2	
3	The IR is intentionally tiny and directly traversable::
4	
5	    Module
6	      Function            (signature, local slots, basic blocks)
7	        Block             (phi nodes, ordered instructions, one terminator)
8	          Phi             (SSA only; one incoming value per predecessor)
9	          Instruction     (Const / Copy / BinOp / Call, all write a dest)
10	          Terminator      (Return / Jump / Branch)
11	
12	Two flavors of module exist:
13	
14	* non-SSA (produced by :func:`lower_module`): value references are
15	  :class:`Temp` -- numbered temporaries produced by instructions -- and
16	  :class:`Slot`, numbered mutable local storage (parameters and ``let``
17	  variables).  Temporaries are mostly single assignment; the sole exception
18	  is the result temporary of a short-circuit boolean operation, which is
19	  written once on each participating path, as is natural in non-SSA form.
20	* SSA (produced by :func:`to_ssa`): every parameter and every instruction
21	  result is a unique definition, slots never appear, and control-flow joins
22	  carry :class:`Phi` nodes listed before the block's ordinary instructions.
23	
24	Both flavors reuse the same node classes; a module's ``ssa`` flag (and each
25	function's) says which one it is.
26	"""
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
30	from typing import Optional, Union
31	
32	
33	@dataclass(frozen=True)
34	class Temp:
35	    id: int
36	    type: str
37	
38	    def __str__(self) -> str:
39	        return f"%t{self.id}"
40	
41	
42	@dataclass(frozen=True)
43	class Slot:
44	    """A mutable local slot (parameter or ``let`` variable)."""
45	
46	    id: int
47	    type: str
48	
49	    def __str__(self) -> str:
50	        return f"%v{self.id}"
51	
52	
53	ValueRef = Union[Temp, Slot]
54	
55	
56	@dataclass
57	class Const:
58	    dest: Temp
59	    value: Union[int, bool]
60	
61	    @property
62	    def op(self) -> str:
63	        return "const"
64	
65	
66	@dataclass
67	class Copy:
68	    dest: Union[Temp, Slot]
69	    src: ValueRef
70	
71	    @property
72	    def op(self) -> str:
73	        return "copy"
74	
75	
76	@dataclass
77	class BinOp:
78	    dest: Temp
79	    operator: str
80	    left: ValueRef
81	    right: ValueRef
82	    kind: str  # "arith" or "compare"
83	    type: str  # result type
84	
85	    @property
86	    def op(self) -> str:
87	        return self.kind
88	
89	
90	@dataclass
91	class Call:
92	    dest: Temp
93	    name: str
94	    args: list[ValueRef]
95	    type: str
96	
97	    @property
98	    def op(self) -> str:
99	        return "call"
100	
101	
102	Instruction = Union[Const, Copy, BinOp, Call]
103	
104	
105	@dataclass(eq=False)
106	class Phi:
107	    """An SSA phi function: merges definitions from predecessor blocks.
108	
109	    ``entries`` maps a predecessor :class:`Block` to the value that is live
110	    on that edge.  Entries are kept sorted by predecessor label whenever a
111	    module is emitted by :func:`to_ssa`; only reachable predecessors occur.
112	    """
113	
114	    dest: Temp
115	    entries: dict["Block", ValueRef] = field(default_factory=dict)
116	
117	    @property
118	    def op(self) -> str:
119	        return "phi"
120	
121	    @property
122	    def type(self) -> str:
123	        return self.dest.type
124	
125	
126	@dataclass
127	class Return:
128	    value: Optional[ValueRef]
129	
130	    @property
131	    def op(self) -> str:
132	        return "return"
133	
134	
135	@dataclass
136	class Jump:
137	    target: "Block"
138	
139	    @property
140	    def op(self) -> str:
141	        return "jump"
142	
143	
144	@dataclass
145	class Branch:
146	    cond: ValueRef
147	    true_target: "Block"
148	    false_target: "Block"
149	
150	    @property
151	    def op(self) -> str:
152	        return "br"
153	
154	
155	Terminator = Union[Return, Jump, Branch]
156	
157	
158	@dataclass(eq=False)
159	class Block:
160	    id: int
161	    instructions: list[Instruction] = field(default_factory=list)
162	    terminator: Optional[Terminator] = None
163	    # SSA only; empty in non-SSA blocks.  Phi nodes precede the ordinary
164	    # instructions.
165	    phis: list[Phi] = field(default_factory=list)
166	
167	    @property
168	    def label(self) -> str:
169	        return f"b{self.id}"
170	
171	    @property
172	    def is_terminated(self) -> bool:
173	        return self.terminator is not None
174	
175	
176	@dataclass
177	class Parameter:
178	    name: str
179	    slot: Slot
180	    # SSA only: the unique parameter definition.  None in non-SSA functions,
181	    # where the parameter is read through ``slot``.
182	    temp: Optional[Temp] = None
183	
184	
185	@dataclass
186	class Function:
187	    name: str
188	    params: list[Parameter]
189	    ret_type: str
190	    locals: list[Slot]
191	    blocks: list[Block]
192	    entry: Block
193	    ssa: bool = False
194	
195	    def is_void(self) -> bool:
196	        return self.ret_type == "void"
197	
198	
199	@dataclass
200	class Module:
201	    functions: list[Function]
202	    ssa: bool = False
203

"""compiler-ir: AST -> control-flow IR lowering pipeline.

Public entry points
-------------------
* :func:`lower_ir` / :func:`lower_module` -- accept a program AST made of
  plain dicts and lists, run name resolution and type checking, and return
  a traversable non-SSA :class:`Module`.
* :func:`to_ssa` -- convert a :class:`Module` into a brand new, traversable
  pruned-SSA :class:`Module` without mutating the input.
* :func:`eliminate_dead_code` -- remove definitions unreachable from the
  SSA roots (terminator operands and calls) into a brand new SSA
  :class:`Module`, without mutating the input.
* :func:`render_module` -- render either flavor of :class:`Module` to
  deterministic text.
* :func:`emit_ir` -- convenience wrapper combining lowering and rendering.
"""
__version__ = "0.1.0"

from .errors import (
    CompilerError,
    DuplicateSymbolError,
    InvalidAstError,
    MissingReturnError,
    TypeCheckError,
    UndefinedSymbolError,
)
from .ir_nodes import (
    BinOp,
    Block,
    Branch,
    Call,
    Const,
    Copy,
    Function,
    Jump,
    Module,
    Parameter,
    Phi,
    Return,
    Slot,
    Temp,
)
from .lowerer import lower_ir, lower_module
from .printer import render_module
from .ssa import to_ssa
from .dce import eliminate_dead_code


def emit_ir(ast: dict) -> str:
    """Validate, analyze and lower ``ast`` and return its text IR."""
    return render_module(lower_module(ast))


__all__ = [
    "__version__",
    # entry points
    "lower_ir",
    "lower_module",
    "to_ssa",
    "eliminate_dead_code",
    "render_module",
    "emit_ir",
    # IR object model
    "Module",
    "Function",
    "Block",
    "Parameter",
    "Phi",
    "Temp",
    "Slot",
    "Const",
    "Copy",
    "BinOp",
    "Call",
    "Return",
    "Jump",
    "Branch",
    # errors
    "CompilerError",
    "InvalidAstError",
    "DuplicateSymbolError",
    "UndefinedSymbolError",
    "TypeCheckError",
    "MissingReturnError",
]

1	"""Deterministic plain-text rendering of the IR.
2	
3	The output is a direct, fixed-order walk of the IR tree: functions in
4	module order, blocks in id order, phi nodes (SSA only) then instructions in
5	emission order.  Nothing is sorted by name or derived from object identity
6	-- phi entries are ordered by predecessor label, which is itself fixed -- so
7	a given module renders byte-identically across processes and repeated
8	conversions.
9	
10	Non-SSA modules render exactly as before (``%tN`` temporaries, ``%vN``
11	slots).  SSA modules use a distinct representation: every value is a unique
12	``%N`` definition, parameters are rendered with their SSA value, no locals
13	section is emitted, and phi lines carry the result type plus one
14	``[block, value]`` pair per reachable predecessor.
15	"""
16	from .ir_nodes import (
17	    BinOp,
18	    Branch,
19	    Call,
20	    Const,
21	    Copy,
22	    Function,
23	    Jump,
24	    Module,
25	    Phi,
26	    Return,
27	)
28	
29	
30	def _render_instruction(ins, value) -> str:
31	    if isinstance(ins, Const):
32	        literal = "true" if ins.value is True else "false" if ins.value is False else str(ins.value)
33	        return f"    {value(ins.dest)}: {ins.dest.type} = const {literal}"
34	    if isinstance(ins, Copy):
35	        return f"    {value(ins.dest)}: {ins.dest.type} = copy {value(ins.src)}"
36	    if isinstance(ins, BinOp):
37	        return (
38	            f"    {value(ins.dest)}: {ins.type} = {ins.kind} {ins.operator} "
39	            f"{value(ins.left)} {value(ins.right)}"
40	        )
41	    if isinstance(ins, Call):
42	        args = ", ".join(value(a) for a in ins.args)
43	        return f"    {value(ins.dest)}: {ins.type} = call {ins.name}({args})"
44	    raise AssertionError(f"unknown instruction: {ins!r}")  # pragma: no cover
45	
46	
47	def _render_phi(phi: Phi, value) -> str:
48	    sources = ", ".join(
49	        f"[{block.label}, {value(val)}]"
50	        for block, val in sorted(phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id)
51	    )
52	    return f"    {value(phi.dest)}: {phi.type} = phi {sources}"
53	
54	
55	def _render_terminator(term, value) -> str:
56	    if isinstance(term, Return):
57	        if term.value is None:
58	            return "    return"
59	        return f"    return {value(term.value)}"
60	    if isinstance(term, Jump):
61	        return f"    jump {term.target.label}"
62	    if isinstance(term, Branch):
63	        return (
64	            f"    br {value(term.cond)}, {term.true_target.label}, "
65	            f"{term.false_target.label}"
66	        )
67	    raise AssertionError(f"unknown terminator: {term!r}")  # pragma: no cover
68	
69	
70	def _render_function(func: Function) -> str:
71	    ssa = getattr(func, "ssa", False)
72	
73	    if ssa:
74	        def value(v) -> str:
75	            return f"%{v.id}"
76	
77	        params = ", ".join(
78	            f"{p.name}: {p.temp.type} @ {value(p.temp)}" for p in func.params
79	        )
80	    else:
81	        def value(v) -> str:
82	            return str(v)
83	
84	        params = ", ".join(f"{p.name}: {p.slot.type} @ {value(p.slot)}"
85	                           for p in func.params)
86	
87	    lines = [f"function {func.name}({params}) -> {func.ret_type} {{"]
88	    if not ssa and func.locals:
89	        lines.append("  locals:")
90	        for slot in func.locals:
91	            lines.append(f"    {value(slot)}: {slot.type}")
92	    for block in func.blocks:
93	        lines.append(f"  {block.label}:")
94	        if ssa:
95	            for phi in block.phis:
96	                lines.append(_render_phi(phi, value))
97	        for ins in block.instructions:
98	            lines.append(_render_instruction(ins, value))
99	        lines.append(_render_terminator(block.terminator, value))
100	    lines.append("}")
101	    return "\n".join(lines)
102	
103	
104	def render_module(module: Module) -> str:
105	    """Render a :class:`Module` to deterministic plain text."""
106	    parts = ["module"]
107	    parts.extend(_render_function(func) for func in module.functions)
108	    return "\n".join(parts) + "\n"
109

1	"""Dead-code elimination on pruned SSA form.
2	
3	The entry point :func:`eliminate_dead_code` takes an SSA :class:`Module`
4	produced by :func:`~compiler_ir.ssa.to_ssa` and returns a brand new SSA
5	:class:`Module` with unreachable definitions removed; the input module is
6	never mutated and shares no mutable function, block, instruction or phi
7	container with the result.
8	
9	Liveness is traced per function, definition-to-use, from fixed roots:
10	
11	* every operand of a ``Return`` or ``Branch`` terminator;
12	* every ``Call`` instruction, regardless of whether its result is used --
13	  the call itself and its position in the instruction stream are observable
14	  behavior -- together with all of its argument definitions.
15	
16	A ``Const``, ``BinOp`` or ``Phi`` that cannot reach one of those roots is
17	deleted.  The trace runs on the whole function at once, so chains feeding
18	only other dead definitions and closed phi cycles die together in one pass;
19	elimination is then repeated until no new dead definition appears.
20	
21	The pass is purely subtractive.  No constants are folded, branches
22	rewritten, blocks deleted or control flow reordered.  Function order,
23	signatures, parameters, return types, block labels and order, terminators,
24	the relative order of surviving instructions and the predecessor order of
25	surviving phis are all preserved, and SSA numbers of surviving values are
26	left untouched (the output may therefore contain numbering holes).
27	
28	Applying the pass to an already minimal module returns an independent,
29	structurally and textually equivalent copy, so a second
30	:func:`eliminate_dead_code` changes nothing.  A non-:class:`Module` object
31	raises :class:`TypeError`; a non-SSA :class:`Module` raises
32	:class:`ValueError`.
33	"""
34	from .ir_nodes import (
35	    BinOp,
36	    Block,
37	    Branch,
38	    Call,
39	    Const,
40	    Copy,
41	    Function,
42	    Jump,
43	    Module,
44	    Parameter,
45	    Phi,
46	    Return,
47	    Temp,
48	)
49	
50	
51	def eliminate_dead_code(module: Module) -> Module:
52	    """Return a new SSA :class:`Module` with dead definitions removed.
53	
54	    The input module is left untouched; the result shares no mutable
55	    function, block, instruction or phi object with it.
56	
57	    :raises TypeError: if ``module`` is not a :class:`Module` instance.
58	    :raises ValueError: if ``module`` is not in SSA form.
59	    """
60	    if not isinstance(module, Module):
61	        raise TypeError(
62	            "eliminate_dead_code expects a Module, got "
63	            f"{type(module).__name__}"
64	        )
65	    if not getattr(module, "ssa", False):
66	        raise ValueError("eliminate_dead_code expects an SSA Module")
67	    return Module(
68	        [_eliminate_in_function(func) for func in module.functions], ssa=True
69	    )
70	
71	
72	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
73	# Operand helpers (mirror the ones used by the SSA conversion)
74	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
75	
76	
77	def _operands(ins):
78	    if isinstance(ins, BinOp):
79	        return [ins.left, ins.right]
80	    if isinstance(ins, Call):
81	        return list(ins.args)
82	    # Const has no operands; a Copy cannot survive the non-SSA -> SSA
83	    # conversion (it folds into renaming) but is treated as pure anyway.
84	    if isinstance(ins, Copy):
85	        return [ins.src]
86	    return []
87	
88	
89	def _term_operands(term):
90	    if isinstance(term, Return) and term.value is not None:
91	        return [term.value]
92	    if isinstance(term, Branch):
93	        return [term.cond]
94	    return []
95	
96	
97	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	# Per-function elimination
99	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
100	
101	
102	def _live_definitions(func: Function) -> set:
103	    """Return the ids of values live from the terminator/call roots.
104	
105	    Roots are every value read by a ``Return`` or ``Branch`` and *every*
106	    ``Call`` instruction (plus, transitively, its arguments): a call whose
107	    result is unused is still observable.  From each root the use-def graph
108	    -- instruction operands and phi incoming values -- is walked to a
109	    fixpoint, so a value only reachable from dead code or a closed phi
110	    cycle is absent from the result.
111	    """
112	    phi_by_dest: dict = {}
113	    operands_by_dest: dict = {}
114	    worklist: list = []
115	
116	    for block in func.blocks:
117	        for ins in block.instructions:
118	            operands_by_dest[id(ins.dest)] = _operands(ins)
119	            if isinstance(ins, Call):
120	                # The call itself is a root even if its result is unused:
121	                # reaching its dest below also pulls in its arguments.
122	                worklist.append(ins.dest)
123	        worklist.extend(_term_operands(block.terminator))
124	        for phi in block.phis:
125	            phi_by_dest[id(phi.dest)] = phi
126	
127	    live: set = set()
128	    while worklist:
129	        value = worklist.pop()
130	        if value is None or id(value) in live:
131	            continue
132	        live.add(id(value))
133	        phi = phi_by_dest.get(id(value))
134	        if phi is not None:
135	            worklist.extend(phi.entries.values())
136	        else:
137	            worklist.extend(operands_by_dest.get(id(value), ()))
138	    return live
139	
140	
141	def _eliminate_in_function(func: Function) -> Function:
142	    live = _live_definitions(func)
143	
144	    new_blocks = [Block(block.id) for block in func.blocks]
145	    block_map = dict(zip(func.blocks, new_blocks))
146	
147	    # Pre-create one fresh Temp for every surviving definition before
148	    # cloning anything: a phi in an earlier block (e.g. a loop header's
149	    # backedge entry) can reference an instruction defined in a later
150	    # block, and every retained use must resolve to the very same output
151	    # object.  Original ids are kept, so numbering holes from removed
152	    # definitions remain.
153	    value_map: dict = {
154	        id(param.temp): Temp(param.temp.id, param.temp.type)
155	        for param in func.params
156	    }
157	    for block in func.blocks:
158	        for phi in block.phis:
159	            if id(phi.dest) in live:
160	                value_map[id(phi.dest)] = Temp(phi.dest.id, phi.dest.type)
161	        for ins in block.instructions:
162	            if isinstance(ins, Call) or id(ins.dest) in live:
163	                value_map[id(ins.dest)] = Temp(
164	                    ins.dest.id, ins.dest.type
165	                )
166	
167	    def map_value(value):
168	        if value is None:
169	            return None
170	        mapped = value_map.get(id(value))
171	        if mapped is None:
172	            # Defensive: a referenced value with no surviving definition.
173	            # Never occurs for SSA IR produced by to_ssa, where every
174	            # operand of a live construct is itself live.
175	            mapped = Temp(value.id, value.type)
176	            value_map[id(value)] = mapped
177	        return mapped
178	
179	    for block, new_block in zip(func.blocks, new_blocks):
180	        for phi in block.phis:
181	            if id(phi.dest) not in live:
182	                continue
183	            entries = {
184	                block_map[pred]: map_value(value)
185	                for pred, value in sorted(
186	                    phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id
187	                )
188	            }
189	            new_block.phis.append(Phi(map_value(phi.dest), entries))
190	
191	        for ins in block.instructions:
192	            if not isinstance(ins, Call) and id(ins.dest) not in live:
193	                continue
194	            dest = map_value(ins.dest)
195	            if isinstance(ins, Const):
196	                clone = Const(dest, ins.value)
197	            elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
198	                clone = Copy(dest, map_value(ins.src))
199	            elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
200	                clone = BinOp(
201	                    dest, ins.operator, map_value(ins.left),
202	                    map_value(ins.right), ins.kind, ins.type,
203	                )
204	            else:
205	                clone = Call(
206	                    dest, ins.name,
207	                    [map_value(arg) for arg in ins.args], ins.type,
208	                )
209	            new_block.instructions.append(clone)
210	
211	        term = block.terminator
212	        if isinstance(term, Return):
213	            new_block.terminator = Return(map_value(term.value))
214	        elif isinstance(term, Jump):
215	            new_block.terminator = Jump(block_map[term.target])
216	        elif isinstance(term, Branch):
217	            new_block.terminator = Branch(
218	                map_value(term.cond),
219	                block_map[term.true_target],
220	                block_map[term.false_target],
221	            )
222	
223	    new_params = [
224	        Parameter(
225	            param.name,
226	            param.slot,
227	            map_value(param.temp),
228	        )
229	        for param in func.params
230	    ]
231	
232	    return Function(
233	        func.name,
234	        new_params,
235	        func.ret_type,
236	        list(func.locals),
237	        new_blocks,
238	        block_map[func.entry],
239	        ssa=True,
240	    )

1	"""Tests for SSA dead-code elimination (:func:`eliminate_dead_code`).
2	
3	The pass is tested five ways:
4	
5	* the API contract -- new SSA module, input never mutated, ``TypeError``
6	  for non-modules, ``ValueError`` for non-SSA modules, independent copies
7	  for the empty module and already-minimal modules;
8	* root seeding -- ``Call`` instructions (and their argument chains) and
9	  ``Return``/``Branch`` operands survive, while pure ``Const``/``BinOp``
10	  chains feeding nothing observable disappear;
11	* phi handling -- dead phis pinned in ``to_ssa`` output only by dead
12	  instructions, and loop-carried phi cycles, are removed whole, whereas
13	  live phis keep their entries and predecessor order;
14	* preservation -- function/block/terminator/order are untouched, surviving
15	  SSA numbers keep their ids (holes allowed), and every retained reference
16	  resolves inside the output module;
17	* semantics -- the shared IR interpreter executes the eliminated module
18	  and observes the same return value and call sequence as the input.
19	"""
20	import unittest
21	
22	from compiler_ir import (
23	    BinOp,
24	    Block,
25	    Branch,
26	    Call,
27	    Const,
28	    Function,
29	    Jump,
30	    Module,

41	    arith,

44	    compare,

58	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	# Structural helpers
60	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
61	
62	
63	def _edges(block):
64	    term = block.terminator
65	    if isinstance(term, Jump):
66	        return [term.target]
67	    if isinstance(term, Branch):
68	        return [term.true_target, term.false_target]
69	    return []
70	
71	
72	def _operands(ins):
73	    if isinstance(ins, BinOp):
74	        return [ins.left, ins.right]
75	    if isinstance(ins, Call):
76	        return list(ins.args)
77	    return []
78	
79	
80	def _term_operands(term):
81	    if isinstance(term, Return):
82	        return [] if term.value is None else [term.value]
83	    if isinstance(term, Branch):
84	        return [term.cond]
85	    return []
86	
87	
88	def _all_defs(fn_):
89	    defs = [p.temp for p in fn_.params]
90	    for block in fn_.blocks:
91	        defs.extend(phi.dest for phi in block.phis)
92	        defs.extend(ins.dest for ins in block.instructions)
93	    return defs
94	
95	
96	def _all_uses(fn_):
97	    uses = []
98	    for block in fn_.blocks:
99	        for phi in block.phis:
100	            uses.extend(phi.entries.values())
101	        for ins in block.instructions:
102	            uses.extend(_operands(ins))
103	        uses.extend(_term_operands(block.terminator))
104	    return uses
105	
106	
107	def _container_objects(module):
108	    """All mutable container nodes reachable from ``module``."""
109	    types = (Function, Block, Phi, Const, BinOp, Call, Return, Jump,
110	             Branch, Parameter)
111	    found = set()
112	    stack = [module]
113	    while stack:
114	        obj = stack.pop()
115	        if id(obj) in found:
116	            continue
117	        if isinstance(obj, types):
118	            found.add(id(obj))
119	        for attr in vars(obj).values() if hasattr(obj, "__dict__") else ():
120	            if isinstance(attr, types):
121	                stack.append(attr)
122	            elif isinstance(attr, list):
123	                stack.extend(x for x in attr if isinstance(x, types))
124	            elif isinstance(attr, dict):
125	                stack.extend(x for x in attr.values() if isinstance(x, types))
126	    return found
127	
128	
129	def assert_ssa_closed(test, module):
130	    """Every retained use, edge target and phi source lives in the output."""
131	    for fn_ in module.functions:
132	        def_ids = {id(d) for d in _all_defs(fn_)}
133	        block_ids = {id(b) for b in fn_.blocks}
134	        test.assertIn(id(fn_.entry), block_ids)
135	        for block in fn_.blocks:
136	            for phi in block.phis:
137	                for pred, value in phi.entries.items():
138	                    test.assertIn(id(pred), block_ids,
139	                                  "phi source block outside output module")
140	                    test.assertIn(id(value), def_ids,
141	                                  "phi incoming value undefined in output")
142	            for ins in block.instructions:
143	                for value in _operands(ins):
144	                    test.assertIn(id(value), def_ids,
145	                                  f"operand of {ins.op} undefined in output")
146	            for value in _term_operands(block.terminator):
147	                test.assertIn(id(value), def_ids,
148	                              "terminator operand undefined in output")
149	            for target in _edges(block):
150	                test.assertIn(id(target), block_ids,
151	                              "terminator targets block outside output module")

1	"""Pass-ordering and idempotence semantic regression tests.
2	
3	The existing suites pin each pass in isolation (lowering, non-SSA -> SSA,
4	SSA dead-code elimination) and compare non-SSA vs SSA behavior.  This module
5	instead treats the compiler as a *pipeline* made of the existing public
6	entry points and checks that:
7	
8	1. One legal source program, fed through the existing entry point
9	   (:func:`lower_module`, which still runs AST validation, name resolution
10	   and type checking), produces the same observable behavior under the
11	   default optimization pipeline and every alternative *legal* pass order,
12	   using the unoptimized (non-SSA) result as the semantic baseline.
13	2. For fixed source, options and order, repeated compilations are
14	   byte-identical (determinism), while *different* orders are only required
15	   to agree on observable behavior -- never on instruction or text layout.
16	3. Re-applying the same pass sequence to an optimized result changes
17	   neither the canonicalized IR nor the emitted target text (idempotence);
18	   each repeatable pass is also a fixed point on its own.
19	4. Orderings may only permute passes inside the existing stage contracts:
20	   SSA construction precedes every SSA-dependent optimization, and
21	   instruction selection (here, the deterministic :func:`render_module`
22	   emission) runs after IR optimization.
23	
24	Passes and preconditions (nothing new is added to the compiler package)
25	-----------------------------------------------------------------------
26	
27	* ``ssa``  -- :func:`to_ssa`.  Legal on a lowered module and, as an
28	  idempotent canonicalization (clone + deterministic renumbering), on an
29	  already-SSA module.
30	* ``dce``  -- :func:`eliminate_dead_code`.  Its documented precondition is
31	  an SSA module: applying it before ``ssa`` raises ``ValueError``.
32	* instruction selection is the final :func:`render_module` and is fixed
33	  last.
34	
35	The default optimization pipeline is ``ssa, dce, ssa``: the SSA-dependent
36	optimization (DCE) sits after SSA construction, and a trailing SSA
37	canonicalization compacts the numbering holes DCE may leave so the emitted
38	IR is the canonical fixed point of the sequence.  Alternative legal orders
39	differ only in the middle (extra normalization, an extra fixpoint DCE, or an
40	ssa/dce interleaving); the no-DCE order ``ssa`` is legal as well.
41	
42	Observables
43	-----------
44	
45	The language has no I/O statement, so the ordered trace of executed calls
46	``(callee, positional args)`` is the standard-output surrogate -- the only
47	side effect the language can have (it is also the observable used by
48	``test_semantic_equivalence.py``).  An outcome is one of:
49	
50	* normal termination: return value (``None`` for ``void``) + call trace;
51	* a runtime fault: error category, trigger site, the operands at the fault,
52	  and the call trace produced *before* the fault.
53	
54	The language's grammar already includes ``div``/``mod``; the single runtime
55	error the language defines is a zero divisor.  Division and modulo follow
56	truncation toward zero (the remainder satisfies ``a == (a/b)*b + a%b``).
57	There is no array or indexing construct, so no bounds error exists in this
58	language subset, and no undefined-behavior sample is used: every faulting
59	instruction's result is consumed (returned, branched on or accumulated), so
60	no legal order can legally delete it.
61	
62	A fault site is identified independently of SSA numbering by
63	``(function name, block label, operator, ordinal of the BinOp among the
64	BinOps of its block)``: block labels are assigned by the lowering DFS and
65	preserved by ``to_ssa`` and DCE, and the relative order of surviving
66	BinOps is preserved as well.  Every faulting block in this suite contains a
67	single faulting BinOp, so the site is unambiguous.
68	
69	All inputs are fixed literal argument tuples; the pipeline has no random
70	or environment-dependent behavior, hence there is no seed to pin.
71	"""

120	class RuntimeFault(Exception):
121	    """A runtime error defined by the language.
122	
123	    Carries the error ``category``, the numbering-independent ``site``
124	    ``(function, block label, operator, binop ordinal)``, the operand

148	def _trunc_div(a: int, b: int):
149	    """Integer division truncated toward zero; raises ZeroDivisionError."""
150	    if b == 0:
151	        raise ZeroDivisionError

153	    if (a < 0) != (b < 0):
154	        quotient = -quotient
155	    return quotient

159	    """Truncated-toward-zero remainder; raises ZeroDivisionError."""
160	    if b == 0:

352	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch to unknown block "
353	                        f"{target.label}")
354	                previous, block = block, target
355	                continue
356	
357	            _assert(False,
358	                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: unknown terminator")

361	def _apply_binop(instruction: BinOp, left, right, fn_name: str):
362	    if instruction.kind == "arith":
363	        _assert(type(left) is int and type(right) is int,
364	                f"{fn_name}: arithmetic {instruction.operator!r} on "
365	                f"non-int operands {left!r}, {right!r}")
366	        operation = _ARITH.get(instruction.operator)
367	        _assert(operation is not None,
368	                f"{fn_name}: unsupported arithmetic operator "
369	                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
370	        return operation(left, right)
371	
372	    if instruction.kind == "compare":
373	        _assert(type(left) == type(right),
374	                f"{fn_name}: comparison {instruction.operator!r} between "
375	                f"mismatched value types {left!r}, {right!r}")
376	        operation = _COMPARE.get(instruction.operator)
377	        _assert(operation is not None,
378	                f"{fn_name}: unsupported comparison operator "
379	                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
380	        return operation(left, right)
381	
382	    _assert(False, f"{fn_name}: unknown BinOp kind {instruction.kind!r}")

385	class Outcome:
386	    """Observable result of one run: either a normal value or a fault."""
387	
388	    def __init__(self, kind, value=None, output=(), category=None,
389	                 site=None, operands=None):
390	        self.kind = kind  # "normal" | "fault"
391	        self.value = value
392	        self.output = list(output)
393	        self.category = category
394	        self.site = site
395	        self.operands = operands
396	
397	    @classmethod
398	    def normal(cls, value, output):
399	        return cls("normal", value=value, output=output)
400	
401	    @classmethod
402	    def fault(cls, error: RuntimeFault):
403	        return cls(
404	            "fault", output=error.output, category=error.category,
405	            site=error.site, operands=(error.left, error.right),
406	        )
407	
408	    def __eq__(self, other):
409	        if not isinstance(other, Outcome):
410	            return NotImplemented
411	        return (
412	            self.kind, self.value, self.output,
413	            self.category, self.site, self.operands,
414	        ) == (
415	            other.kind, other.value, other.output,
416	            other.category, other.site, other.operands,
417	        )
418	
419	    def __repr__(self):
420	        if self.kind == "normal":
421	            return f"Outcome.normal(value={self.value!r}, output={self.output!r})"
422	        return (
423	            f"Outcome.fault(category={self.category!r}, site={self.site!r}, "
424	            f"operands={self.operands!r}, output={self.output!r})"
425	        )

428	def _interpret(module: Module, entry: str, arguments) -> Outcome:
429	    try:
430	        value, trace = _Interpreter(module).run(entry, arguments)
431	    except RuntimeFault as fault:
432	        return Outcome.fault(fault)
433	    return Outcome.normal(value, trace)

440	
441	# SSA construction, DCE, then a final SSA canonicalization (clone +
442	# deterministic renumbering), which makes the emitted IR the fixed point of
443	# the whole sequence: DCE may leave numbering holes, and the trailing ssa
444	# pass compacts them without changing structure or semantics.
445	DEFAULT_ORDER = ("ssa", "dce", "ssa")
446	
447	# Legal alternatives: extra early normalization, an explicit DCE fixpoint
448	# repeat, and an ssa/dce interleaving -- all end in the canonicalizing ssa
449	# pass, so each is a fixed point of its own sequence.
450	ALT_DOUBLE_SSA = ("ssa", "ssa", "dce", "ssa")
451	ALT_DCE_FIXPOINT = ("ssa", "dce", "dce", "ssa")
452	ALT_INTERLEAVE = ("ssa", "dce", "ssa", "dce", "ssa")
453	# Legal but less optimizing: construction + canonicalization only.
454	NO_DCE_ORDER = ("ssa",)
455	# The README-documented core without the trailing canonicalization: legal,
456	# used for cross-order semantics and determinism (its endpoint may carry
457	# numbering holes and is compared on observables, not text).
458	RAW_CORE_ORDER = ("ssa", "dce")
459	
460	LEGAL_ORDERS = {
461	    "default ssa,dce,ssa": DEFAULT_ORDER,
462	    "alt ssa,ssa,dce,ssa": ALT_DOUBLE_SSA,
463	    "alt ssa,dce,dce,ssa": ALT_DCE_FIXPOINT,
464	    "alt ssa,dce,ssa,dce,ssa": ALT_INTERLEAVE,
465	    "no-dce ssa": NO_DCE_ORDER,
466	    "raw core ssa,dce": RAW_CORE_ORDER,
467	}
468	
469	# Orders whose endpoint is the canonical fixed point used by the strict
470	# idempotence test.
471	IDEMPOTENT_ORDERS = {
472	    name: order for name, order in LEGAL_ORDERS.items()
473	    if name != "raw core ssa,dce"
474	}

477	def apply_order(module: Module, order) -> Module:
478	    """Apply ``order`` (a tuple of pass names) to ``module``.
479	
480	    :raises ValueError: if a pass name is unknown, if instruction selection
481	        appears anywhere but the end, or if ``dce`` is scheduled before the
482	        first ``ssa`` (DCE requires an SSA module).
483	    """
484	    ssa_seen = bool(getattr(module, "ssa", False))
485	    for index, name in enumerate(order):
486	        if name == "ssa":
487	            module = to_ssa(module)
488	            ssa_seen = True
489	        elif name == "dce":
490	            if not ssa_seen:
491	                raise ValueError(
492	                    "pass order violates precondition: 'dce' requires an SSA "
493	                    "module, but no 'ssa' pass precedes it"
494	                )
495	            module = eliminate_dead_code(module)
496	        elif name == "isel":
497	            raise ValueError(
498	                "pass order violates stage contract: instruction selection "
499	                "('isel') must be the final stage"
500	            )
501	        else:
502	            raise ValueError(f"unknown pass in order: {name!r}")
503	    return module
504

506	def compile_ast(ast: dict, order):
507	    """Compile a fresh copy of ``ast`` through lowering and ``order``.
508	
509	    Returns ``(unoptimized_module, optimized_module, target_text)`` where
510	    the target text is instruction selection (rendering) run last.
511	    """
512	    lowered = lower_module(copy.deepcopy(ast))
513	    optimized = apply_order(lowered, order)
514	    return lowered, optimized, render_module(optimized)

517	def structural_signature(module: Module):
518	    """Numbering-independent structural fingerprint of a module."""
519	    signature = []
520	    for fn_ in module.functions:
521	        blocks = []
522	        for block in fn_.blocks:
523	            instructions = []
524	            for ins in block.instructions:
525	                if isinstance(ins, Const):
526	                    instructions.append(("const", ins.value))
527	                elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
528	                    instructions.append(("copy",))
529	                elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
530	                    instructions.append((ins.kind, ins.operator))
531	                elif isinstance(ins, Call):
532	                    instructions.append(("call", ins.name, len(ins.args)))
533	            terminator = type(block.terminator).__name__
534	            blocks.append((
535	                block.id, terminator, len(block.phis),
536	                tuple(instructions),
537	            ))
538	        signature.append((
539	            fn_.name, fn_.ret_type,
540	            tuple((p.name, p.temp.type if p.temp is not None
541	                   else p.slot.type) for p in fn_.params),
542	            tuple(blocks),
543	        ))
544	    return tuple(signature)

552	def _emit_function(name="emit"):
553	    return func(name, [param("v", "int")], "int", [ret(var("v"))])

556	# A) Constants and phi propagation at a branch convergence.
557	#
558	# `a` is the same dominating constant on BOTH outgoing edges, so its merge
559	# phi is trivial (one incoming SSA value) and is pruned during SSA
560	# construction; the returned value is that constant propagated through the
561	# join.  `b` carries genuinely different values per edge and needs a real
562	# merge phi consumed by a side-effecting call.
563	def _join_program():
564	    return program(
565	        func("join", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
566	            let("k", "int", int_(7)),
567	            let("a", "int", int_(0)),
568	            if_(var("c"), [assign("a", var("k"))],
569	                 [assign("a", var("k"))]),
570	            let("b", "int", int_(0)),
571	            if_(var("c"),
572	                [assign("b", arith("add", var("x"), int_(1)))],
573	                [assign("b", arith("sub", var("x"), int_(1)))]),
574	            let("s", "int", call("emit", [var("b")])),
575	            ret(arith("add", var("a"), var("s"))),
576	        ]),
577	        _emit_function(),
578	    )
579	
580	
581	# B) Deletable pure computations vs. still-side-effecting expressions.
582	#
583	# `d` and `junk` are pure chains nobody consumes: DCE deletes them (and
584	# their constants), but BOTH calls remain roots even though `ignored`'s
585	# result is never read -- deleting either would drop observable output.
586	def _clean_program():
587	    return program(
588	        func("clean", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
589	            let("d", "int",
590	                arith("mul", arith("add", int_(1), int_(2)), int_(3))),
591	            let("keptarg", "int", arith("add", var("n"), int_(10))),
592	            let("v", "int", call("observe", [var("keptarg")])),
593	            let("ignored", "int", call("observe", [int_(99)])),
594	            let("junk", "int",
595	                arith("add", arith("mul", var("v"), int_(3)), var("d"))),
596	            ret(arith("add", var("v"), int_(4))),
597	        ]),
598	        _emit_function("observe"),
599	    )
600	
601	
602	# C) Loop-invariant value plus a conditional branch inside the loop.
603	#
604	# `base` is loop invariant and defined before the header; the loop still
605	# carries real header phis for `i` and `total`, and the in-loop if makes the
606	# side-effecting call happen only on iterations that take its else edge.
607	def _loop_program():
608	    return program(
609	        func("loopsum", [param("n", "int"), param("k", "int")], "int", [
610	            let("base", "int", arith("add", var("k"), int_(1))),
611	            let("total", "int", int_(0)),
612	            let("i", "int", int_(0)),
613	            while_(compare("lt", var("i"), var("n")), [
614	                if_(compare("gt", var("i"), int_(1)),
615	                    [assign("total", arith(
616	                        "add",
617	                        arith("add", var("total"), var("base")),
618	                        var("i")))],
619	                    [
620	                        let("t", "int", call("ping", [var("i")])),
621	                        assign("total", arith("add", var("total"), var("t"))),
622	                    ]),
623	                assign("i", arith("add", var("i"), int_(1))),
624	            ]),
625	            ret(var("total")),
626	        ]),
627	        _emit_function("ping"),
628	    )
629	
630	
631	# D) An inlineable call with dead code introduced after it.
632	#
633	# `dbl` is a trivial inline candidate; no pass order actually inlines it, so
634	# every order keeps the call and its observable position.  The pure
635	# computations built AFTER the call (`junk1`, `junk2`) are dead and vanish
636	# under DCE, while the later side-effecting call `after` is preserved.
637	def _around_program():
638	    return program(
639	        func("around", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
640	            let("v", "int", call("dbl", [arith("add", var("n"), int_(1))])),
641	            let("junk1", "int", arith("mul", var("v"), int_(9))),
642	            let("junk2", "int", arith("add", var("junk1"), int_(5))),
643	            let("w", "int", call("after", [var("v")])),
644	            ret(var("v")),
645	        ]),
646	        func("dbl", [param("x", "int")], "int",
647	             [ret(arith("mul", var("x"), int_(2)))]),
648	        _emit_function("after"),
649	    )
650	
651	
652	# E1) Zero divisor on one arm of a branch; the other arm terminates fine.
653	def _guarded_fault_program():
654	    return program(
655	        func("guarded", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
656	            let("d", "int", int_(0)),
657	            if_(var("c"),
658	                [
659	                    let("e", "int", call("emit", [int_(1)])),
660	                    let("q", "int", arith("div", var("x"), var("d"))),
661	                    ret(arith("add", var("q"), var("e"))),
662	                ],
663	                [
664	                    let("e2", "int", call("emit", [int_(2)])),
665	                    ret(var("e2")),
666	                ]),
667	        ]),
668	        _emit_function(),
669	    )

672	# E2) Zero divisor reached inside a loop after observable output.
673	def _loop_fault_program():
674	    return program(
675	        func("looptrap", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
676	            let("total", "int", int_(0)),
677	            let("i", "int", int_(0)),
678	            while_(compare("lt", var("i"), var("n")), [
679	                let("e", "int", call("emit", [var("i")])),

681	                    arith("div", int_(100),

684	                assign("i", arith("add", var("i"), int_(1))),

699	            ret(arith("add", var("r"), var("e"))),

797	def _first_difference(expected: Outcome, actual: Outcome):
798	    """Name the first observable that differs, in comparison order."""
799	    if expected.kind != actual.kind:
800	        return "termination kind", expected.kind, actual.kind
801	    if expected.output != actual.output:
802	        return "standard output (ordered call trace)", expected.output, \
803	            actual.output
804	    if expected.kind == "fault":
805	        if expected.category != actual.category:
806	            return "runtime error category", expected.category, \
807	                actual.category
808	        if expected.site != actual.site:
809	            return "runtime error trigger site", expected.site, actual.site
810	        if expected.operands != actual.operands:
811	            return "runtime error operands", expected.operands, \
812	                actual.operands
813	    else:
814	        if expected.value != actual.value:
815	            return "return value", expected.value, actual.value
816	    return None

819	def _mismatch_message(label, order_name, entry, arguments, expected, actual):
820	    diff = _first_difference(expected, actual)
821	    header = (
822	        f"semantic mismatch for sample {label!r}, order {order_name!r}, "
823	        f"entry {entry!r}, arguments {arguments!r}"
824	    )
825	    if diff is None:
826	        return header
827	    field, wanted, got = diff
828	    return (
829	        f"{header}\n"
830	        f"first differing observable: {field}\n"
831	        f"  expected: {wanted!r}\n"
832	        f"  actual:   {got!r}\n"
833	        f"baseline outcome: {expected!r}\n"
834	        f"this order:       {actual!r}"
835	    )
